nodes.title: Oak’s meridian reading
nodes.summary: Oak interprets Arundhatī being ahead of Vasiṣṭha as Alcor crossing the north–south meridian first.

nodes.title: Meridian
nodes.summary: The north–south line through the point directly above an observer. Crossing its upper part is the transit compared in the benchmark.

nodes.title: Nakshatra
nodes.summary: In the calendar, one of 27 equal sectors along the Moon’s path. In a literary sky passage, the named group or asterism needs its own interpretation.

nodes.title: The birth of Rāma
nodes.summary: Compare the brief Baroda passage with the longer Southern Recension passage, which names the lunar day and identifies the asterism by its presiding deity.

nodes.title: Southern Recension
nodes.summary: A transmitted family of readings. The birth comparison identifies the IIT Kanpur text and uses that text’s own numbering.

nodes.title: Calculate the daily calendar
nodes.summary: Pick a city and date. Look up the Moon’s nakshatra at sunrise and see when it changes.

nodes.title: Raigad
nodes.summary: A hill fort and capital site. The terrain lesson follows a modern elevation transect across the fort.

nodes.title: The coronation at Raigad
nodes.summary: The atlas places Shivaji Maharaj’s 1674 coronation at the fort and introduces its role as a capital.

nodes.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre
nodes.summary: Maintains the official inscription record and maps for the property that includes Raigad.

edges.why: Oak identifies the pair with Alcor and Mizar and supplies a geometric rule for the story’s relative position.

edges.scope: Modern mean geometry and separate historical scenarios
edges.why: The modern benchmark checks the upper-transit calculation on a known date. The historical sweep awaits independent review.
Local sidereal time connects the observer’s meridian to a star’s right ascension.
The reference to Aditi is read as Punarvasu. The corresponding Baroda main-text line is briefer.
This recension preserves the fuller astronomical description of the birth.

edges.scope: Modern calendar, sunrise at selected city
edges.why: The calculator assigns the Moon’s sidereal longitude to one of the 27 sectors and gives the next change.
The fort is the documented capital and coronation location in the heritage record.
Raigad is one of twelve components in the inscribed military landscapes.
The article illustrates Oak’s transit-order reading on his proposed date and in a modern comparison. Both figures express the author’s interpretation.
Raigad’s site record describes rainwater storage. The district history describes how loss of access to food affected a campaign camp at Panipat. Both help a reader ask how a place was provisioned.
